A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PowerCLIP study. All 18 pages of each version, including figures, tables, theoretical proofs, and empirical appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, retrieval, robustness, compositionality, ablation, approximation-accuracy, and computational-cost results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results and adds a loss-weight ablation and OV-COCO evaluation in Tables 14–15.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same region and phrase embeddings, bidirectional powerset alignment, CLIP-plus-triplet objective, and two nonlinear aggregators. The added loss-weight study introduces no new algorithmic component; its conflicting setting statements are addressed under E3.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds open-vocabulary object-detection evaluation on OV-COCO, reporting performance on base and novel categories. This introduces substantially different task requirements from v1's COCO image-text retrieval evaluation. Existing training data and other evaluation coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain their baseline membership. The new OV-COCO comparison uses CLIP, FLIP, FILIP, SPARC, and C-PGS, the same comparator set already evaluated together in the Winoground comparison in Table 5.

E3.justification: v3 adds a λ sweep over 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 and OV-COCO reporting of base, novel, and overall AP50. Appendix F states that all experiments use λ = 0.1, conflicting with the retained λ = 0.2 in Section 3.4. This does not establish that earlier experiments were rerun or their actual settings changed.

E4.justification: Appendix F and Table 14 add sensitivity analysis for the triplet-loss mixing coefficient, comparing classification and retrieval performance. Existing component, mask, activation, approximation, robustness, computational-cost, and qualitative analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures are added or revised. New tables continue reporting point estimates, and the existing correlation analyses are retained.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–13 and plotted findings are retained. New Table 14 reports classification/retrieval scores of 42.2/47.0, 40.7/47.6, and 41.3/47.1 for λ = 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3. New Table 15 reports PowerCLIP versus CLIP at 24.4 versus 17.2 overall AP50 and 15.3 versus 1.4 novel-category AP50. These are additional results, not established same-setting revisions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorems 1–2, Corollary 1, and proofs in Appendices A–B are unchanged. The added experiments introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: powerset alignment, tractable NLA approximations, and improved compositionality, robustness, and zero-shot performance. The new appendix evidence does not revise these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly interprets retrieval as relatively stable across λ and classification as more sensitive, motivating λ = 0.1 as a trade-off. Appendix G interprets the OV-COCO gains as evidence of finer visual-text correspondences, particularly for novel categories. Existing interpretations and future-work discussion remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds documentation of tested loss weights and a preferred λ = 0.1, although Section 3.4 still specifies 0.2. Other implementation settings, computational-cost information, and the promised code release are unchanged. The new OV-COCO results lack corresponding implementation and adaptation details.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zareian et al., 'Open-vocabulary object detection using captions' (2021), as the reference for OV-COCO. The related-work narrative and positioning otherwise remain unchanged; subsequent reference-number changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: v3 adds two short appendix sections, relabels the retained Qualitative Examples section from F to H, expands acknowledgements, and adds a computational-cost cross-reference. The main exposition is otherwise unchanged. The new cross-reference incorrectly points to Section 7 rather than Appendix E.

P2.justification: Tables 14–15 are added on the existing computational-cost appendix page, and the qualitative discussion and bibliography reflow. Existing figures and Tables 1–13 are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: Tables 14–15 provide useful additional sensitivity and open-vocabulary evidence. However, v3 introduces conflicting statements about the loss weight used for all experiments—0.1 in Appendix F versus 0.2 in Section 3.4—while retaining the earlier scores, and supplies little procedural detail for OV-COCO. These reproducibility and interpretation problems make the net quality benefit uncertain.
